chapter_theme: One song at Valivalam (வலிவலம்): the poet confesses to common women who leave one man for another with more wealth, and to delighting in house, wife, kin and wealth as if they were permanent, and asks to be set among devotees who worship with flowers.

838.reading: The poet speaks of common women who, though the young man who joined them from the first day is still there, go to another if they find more wealth with him, and of his own failure, caught in their snare and in deeds Brahma wrote, to wear ash and say 'Hara Hara'; he calls himself a poor fool who rejoices that house, wife, kin and wealth are permanent, and asks to be placed with the devotees offering flowers, to reach the higher state and worship the red-jewelled anklets of the feet on the peacock. The praise names Rama, who cut Ravana's crowns with one arrow, Siva of erukku, konrai, Ganga, crescent and bone garland, the vel that crushed Nirudan who stood as a mango tree, and the kadamba garland wet from Valli's breasts, at Valivalam.
838.nuance: அடுத்த பேர் மனை துணைவியர் தமர் பொருள் பெருத்த வாழ்விது சதமென மகிழ்வுறும் அசட்டன்: the confession turns from the women to household attachment, taking house, wife, kin and wealth for permanent (சதம்). The opening lines on the woman and the young man (தொடுத்த நாள் முதல் மருவிய இளைஞனும் இருக்க) are hard to divide, and the reading of them is tentative.

links.note: Both picture the courtesan whose mind is with another man while she embraces this one; the Naladiyar marvels that men still don't see it, and 838 says she leaves the lover of many days as soon as another brings more wealth.
